title: Crosswalking model behavior and enterprise adoption profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Produce an actionable crosswalk that maps observable model behavior patterns (latency distribution, token-efficiency, hallucination classes, instruction-following variance, output determinism at different temperatures, failure modes on RAG / long-context) to enterprise adoption profiles (SLOs, compliance constraints, cost buckets, throughput needs) and procurement decision thresholds. Deliver a small set of vendor-agnostic signals, a scoring rubric, and prioritized shortlist recommendations to inform Dedicated/Private procurement, fallback orchestration, and model onboarding policies.

Why now: Procurement conversations repeatedly surface confusion about which model attributes matter for different enterprise buyers (e.g., finserv vs. SMB search). We need a reproducible way to translate runtime telemetry and qualitative model tests into procurement triggers and rollout constraints so sales and platform teams can recommend appropriate flavors (quantized variants, short-context vs long-context) and fallback strategies.

Outcomes: (1) a spreadsheet of model-behavior fingerprints with normalized metrics and tags; (2) an adoption-profile matrix (security, latency, cost-sensitivity, accuracy tolerance); (3) a scoring rubric that outputs an "enterprise-fit" verdict and recommended deployment mode (hosted / dedicated / private); (4) a short list of 6 prioritized supplier + variant pairings for Q2 pilots; (5) slide deck for GTM and infra stakeholders with 3 playbook examples (RAG search, low-latency chat, document extraction).
research_plan: Inventory telemetry: collect token-level latency distribution, error rates, and KV cache hit rates across top-10 models used in hosted and dedicated environments.
Synthetic probes: run 2000-case suite per model across three workloads (short-chat, RAG-100k, extraction) to categorize hallucination/failure modes and sensitivity to temperature/penalty settings.
Customer signal ingestion: correlate 6 months of support tickets and onboarding surveys for enterprise customers to extract non-functional priorities (SLOs, compliance, throughput).
Expert interviews: 4 sessions with solutions engineers, 3 with sales leads (finserv, health, ecommerce) to validate profile attributes and edge constraints.
Normalize metrics: create per-token cost proxy, per-request latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), and an "accuracy friction" proxy based on domain hallucination scoring.
Produce scoring rubric: weight attributes by customer segment to generate adoption-fit scores and deployment recommendations.
tasks: Define telemetry schema and request data pull from infra (ENG telemetry owner: @sylvia-chen).
Design and finalize 2000-case synthetic probe set (PM + Research to agree).
Run probes and ingest results into sheet (estimate 3 days of compute).
Run qualitative interviews and synthesize adoption attributes.
Draft scoring rubric and validate with 2 solution engineers.
Produce shortlist and recommended pilot pairings with cost/latency estimates.
Create 12-slide GTM + infra handoff deck and review with Head of Sales.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable spreadsheet exists with model fingerprints (latency percentiles, token-cost proxy, KV/cache behavior, failure-mode tags) for at least 8 candidate models/variants.
Adoption-profile matrix completed with segment weights for finserv, healthcare, ecommerce, and SMBs.
Scoring rubric generates a deterministic adoption-fit score for any (model, variant, workload) tuple and yields a recommended deployment mode.
Three example playbooks (RAG search, low-latency chat, batch extraction) show recommended model variants and fallback policies with estimated unit economics.
Deck reviewed and approved by infra lead and sales lead; pilot shortlist accepted by PM org.
